I read `DeligneDatum.tmul_mulVec_mem` in Def_CerednikDrinfeld_FormalUpperHalfPlaneFunctor.lean (lines 122–147). It has the same "push a sum `line ⊔ 𝔭•⊤` through a B-linear map" argument, and it also appears in the `hψ𝔭` block near line 308. I also checked Mathlib's `Submodule.map_smul''`. I did not look at the other 15 files that mention `inclBaseChange B hle`, so more uses may exist. I did not compile anything. The generic lemma below is a sketch. findings.problem: The proof of `hpush` pushes a membership `x ∈ L ⊔ 𝔭 • ⊤` through a B-linear map. It splits the sum with `Submodule.mem_sup`, sends the line part into the target line, and shows the `𝔭 • ⊤` part stays in `𝔭 • ⊤` by `Submodule.smul_induction_on` (smul case and add case). `DeligneDatum.tmul_mulVec_mem` repeats the same steps with `Φ` in place of `inclBaseChange B hle`. Its lines 137–147 have the same `mem_sup` split, the same `smul_induction_on` with `smul_mem_smul hr mem_top`, and the same `add_mem` step. Only the map and the line-membership step differ. The `hψ𝔭` block near line 308 of the same file repeats the `smul_induction_on` skeleton for ideals. Mathlib already states the underlying fact as `Submodule.map_smul''`, so each use re-proves an existing lemma by hand.
findings.proposed_change:
Add one helper next to the definitions, for example
`lemma map_mem_sup_smul_top {P Q} [AddCommGroup P] [Module B P] [AddCommGroup Q] [Module B Q] (Φ : P →ₗ[B] Q) {L : Submodule B P} {L' : Submodule B Q} (hL : ∀ y ∈ L, Φ y ∈ L') {x : P} (hx : x ∈ L ⊔ (𝔭 • ⊤ : Submodule B P)) : Φ x ∈ L' ⊔ (𝔭 • ⊤ : Submodule B Q)`.
Proof sketch: split `x = y + z` with `Submodule.mem_sup`. Then `Φ y ∈ L'` by `hL`. For the other part, `Φ z ∈ Submodule.map Φ (𝔭 • ⊤) = 𝔭 • (⊤.map Φ) ≤ 𝔭 • ⊤` by `Submodule.map_smul''` and `Submodule.smul_mono_right`, which replaces both `smul_induction_on` blocks.
In `solution`, `hpush` becomes `map_mem_sup_smul_top (inclBaseChange B hle) (fun y hy => d.mono hle (Submodule.mem_map_of_mem hy)) hmem`. In `tmul_mulVec_mem`, the `rw [← key]` step is followed by the same lemma applied to `Φ` (as a linear map via `toLinearMap`), with `hL` given by `line_transport` and `mem_comap`.
findings.benefit: The `mem_sup` split and the `smul_induction_on` induction are written once and checked once. Each caller keeps only the hypothesis that its map sends the line into the target line. `solution` shrinks from about 10 lines of induction to one lemma call. A future change to the `𝔭 • ⊤` handling, such as a different `line` type, is made in one place instead of in each file that copies this pattern.
